findings.title: Same NPE remains in the other getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body: The PR makes getSubGroupsCount() null-safe against `modelSupplier.get()` returning null when the group was concurrently deleted. The three getSubGroupsStream overloads (lines 256, 262, 268) still call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` with no null check. The same race (group deleted between cache hit and lazy DB load) still throws an NPE there. The fix is partial. Those overloads should handle null, for example by returning an empty stream or throwing a meaningful exception.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount now returns null for a vanished group, which callers may not expect
findings.body: When the group no longer exists, getSubGroupsCount() returns null instead of failing. The null flows into GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount and from there into the representation, so the API silently reports a missing count. Any other caller that unboxes the Long will NPE instead. A deleted group probably should be skipped or reported as not found, not given a null count. The null contract is undocumented.

findings.title: Concurrency test is racy, never joins the reader thread, and may not hit the fixed path
findings.body: The reader thread is started but never joined. After `deletedAll.set(true)`, the assertion on caughtExceptions can run while the reader is mid-request. An exception thrown in that last in-flight iteration is then missed, and the thread can outlive the test. The reader also calls `groups(null, 0, MAX, true)` with the brief representation, and it is not clear this reaches GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount(). That method is only called when subGroupsCount is requested. The test therefore may not exercise the changed code and may pass without the fix. The test is also inherently timing-dependent. It should join the thread (or use an executor) and request the sub-group count.
